name: Newport
summary: The Gilded Age's summer capital — Vanderbilt 'cottages' on the cliffs, a legendary shore walk, and America's yachting history. New England's final stop before New York.

lodging.name: A Newport harbor inn
lodging.blurb: Colonial inns walkable to the wharves and Bellevue Avenue.

foodMustTry.name: Fresh oysters & stuffies on the wharf
foodMustTry.blurb: Rhode Island 'stuffies' (stuffed quahogs) and raw bar on the water.

days.label: Day 67 — The Breakers & the Cliff Walk
days.summary: The grandest mansion and the walk along the sea.

item.title: The Breakers
item.blurb: The Vanderbilts' 70-room Gilded-Age palace above the Atlantic — the definitive Newport mansion tour.

item.title: The Cliff Walk
item.blurb: A 3.5-mile path between the mansion lawns and the crashing sea.

days.label: Day 68 — Bellevue & Ocean Drive
days.summary: More mansions, the tennis hall of fame, and the scenic loop.

item.title: Marble House & The Elms
item.blurb: Two more Bellevue Avenue palaces — Marble House's gold ballroom and The Elms' formal gardens.

item.title: Ocean Drive & the Tennis Hall of Fame
item.blurb: The 10-mile scenic coastal loop, plus the Victorian Casino and the International Tennis Hall of Fame.

days.label: Day 69 — Leave New England for New York
days.summary: The long drive south that closes the region and opens the Mid-Atlantic.

commute.scenicNote: South through Connecticut along the shoreline — New England gives way to the biggest city on the trip.
